data.name: Gibraltar
data.region: Southern Europe (Iberian peninsula), British Overseas Territory, outside the EU
data.summary: No capital gains tax (except, from 2025, property dealing by owners of five or more taxable properties), no tax on interest, no inheritance, estate, gift or wealth tax. An ordinarily resident individual is taxed on foreign employment and self-employment income and on 'other income' (Income Tax Act 2010 s. 11(2), Sch. 1 Tables B and C), but dividends from companies listed on a Recognised Stock Exchange, or paid out of profits on which Gibraltar charged no tax, are excluded from the charge (Table C Class 1(a)(iii)-(iv)), so a portfolio of foreign shares produces no Gibraltar tax for a resident. Income tax (up to 39% / 28%) bites mainly on Gibraltar-source and employment income. Category 2 (high-net-worth) status excludes foreign dividends from assessable income (Rule 10(1)), caps assessable income at GBP 118,000 and charges a minimum tax of GBP 37,000 a year; one certificate can cover spouse and children (Rule 11). From June 2026 new applicants need GBP 5 million net assets (was GBP 2 million).

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.description: Income tax on income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar, plus certain foreign income for ordinarily resident individuals; two systems (Allowances Based: top rate 39%; Gross Income Based: top rate 25-28%), taxpayer pays the lower. No tax on capital gains or interest.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if present 183 days in a tax year, or more than 300 days in aggregate over three consecutive tax years. Requires a Gibraltar residence permit or Category 2 certificate.

capital_gains.summary: No tax on capital gains. Exception from 1 Jan 2025: profits on selling Gibraltar property (and shares in property-holding entities) are taxable if the person holds, directly or indirectly, five or more taxable properties (or did so over five consecutive periods); primary residence and estate disposals excluded. The Income Tax Act 2010 has no charge on capital gains: Schedule 1 charges only the heads in Tables A to C and, from 1 Jan 2025, profits from residential property disposals (Part 2).

dividends.summary: Under s. 11(2) of the Income Tax Act 2010 an ordinarily resident individual is chargeable on Table B and Table C income arising or received outside Gibraltar. Table C Class 1(a) charges dividends except those paid (i) by a company to another company, (ii) to a person not ordinarily resident, (iii) by a company whose shares are listed on a Recognised Stock Exchange, or (iv) out of profits or gains on which no tax has been charged under the Act, to the extent of those profits. Dividends from foreign listed companies, and from foreign companies whose profits Gibraltar never charged, are therefore untaxed. Income from funds marketed to the public is not charged (Class 2(a)); interest is not a head of charge. Dividends from unlisted Gibraltar companies are taxed to the extent of taxable underlying profits, with a tax credit.
dividends.important_exceptions: The Commissioner designates Recognised Stock Exchanges by Gazette notice; the notice was not found, so listing on a given exchange is not confirmed (limb (iv) would still exempt dividends from foreign profits that Gibraltar did not tax). Dividends from private foreign companies or from non-public funds follow the entity rules.

open_questions: The Gazette notice designating Recognised Stock Exchanges (Income Tax Act 2010 interpretation section and Sch. 1 Table C Class 1(a)) was not found; limb (iv) covers dividends out of profits not charged to Gibraltar tax in any case.
dividends.rate_basis: Foreign listed shares: Table C Class 1(a)(iii) and (iv) of Schedule 1 exclude the dividend from the charge, so 0. Gibraltar company dividends: taxed at personal rates (up to 39%) to the extent of taxable underlying profits, with a tax credit; domestic_rate left null. Domestic rate 0: the family's 'domestic' share of the portfolio is taken as shares listed on a Recognised Stock Exchange, whose dividends are outside assessable income under the same Table C Class 1(a)(iii); Gibraltar has almost no listed companies of its own.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends (general knowledge, not verified).
dividends.treaty_network: Essentially no comprehensive double tax treaties (UK-Gibraltar treaty signed 2019 only); full non-treaty WHT on foreign dividends (not verified).

regimes.name: Category 2 high-net-worth individual
regimes.description: Assessable income is capped at GBP 118,000 a year (Rule 9(4)(a)) and charged only under the Allowances Based System (Rule 9(3), 9(5)); minimum tax GBP 37,000 a year (Rule 9(4)(b)); maximum tax GBP 42,380 at current rates (Income Tax Office). Dividends, pensions and emoluments from outside Gibraltar are not taken into account (Rule 10(1)); Gibraltar rents and permitted Gibraltar business or employment income are assessable (Rule 10(3)-(4)). For a passive foreign portfolio the tax is therefore the GBP 37,000 minimum: the regime buys a residence route and certainty, not a saving over ordinary residence, where the same portfolio is untaxed.
regimes.eligibility: Not present in Gibraltar more than 183 days in any of the last five years or on average 90 days in any three, and no trade, business or employment there in that period (Rule 4); approved residential accommodation in Gibraltar for exclusive use for the whole year (Rule 3); the Finance Centre Director must be satisfied of substantial and sound financial standing and good character (Rule 6). Net assets of GBP 5 million for new applicants from June 2026 (GBP 2 million before): announced by the government on 18 June 2026; the Rules themselves set no figure, and existing holders are grandfathered.
regimes.duration_note: The certificate is effective for an indefinite period (Rule 6) while the holder keeps meeting the conditions of Rules 3, 5 and 7 (accommodation, good standing, taxes and the minimum paid) and submits it for endorsement every three years (Rule 7(3)). It lapses if the holder declares no Gibraltar tax liability (Rule 7(4)).

lump_sum.notes: Minimum tax GBP 37,000 for every year after the year of application (Rule 9(4)(b); GBP 3,083.33 a month in the first and last year, 9(4)(c)-(d)). The tax is the greater of the minimum and the Allowances Based tax on the first GBP 118,000 of assessable income, which is GBP 42,380 at the cap (Income Tax Office). Foreign dividends, pensions and emoluments are outside assessable income unless the holder elects to include them (Rule 10(1)-(2)); capital gains are not taxed in Gibraltar. Gibraltar rents and permitted Gibraltar work are assessable on top (Rule 10(3)-(5)); the lump_sum 'covers' list therefore no longer includes domestic income (earlier version of this file did). A spouse and children can be treated as part of the holder's income by an election (Rule 11(1)), or apply for their own certificate (Rule 11(5)), so one certificate and one minimum can cover the family. An advance payment equal to the maximum tax under Rule 9(4)(a) is due by 30 November and is refundable on surrender (Rule 8); the application fee is GBP 1,233, rising to GBP 5,000 (press release 469/2026). Not indexed by law: amounts changed only by Legal Notice (last LN 2022/173).

succession.name: Gibraltar
succession.summary: Gibraltar has no forced heirship and applies English-style rules. Trusts are fully recognised and the Hague Trusts Convention was extended to Gibraltar. Private foundations are available under a 2017 law.
succession.family_claims: Gibraltar has an English-style family provision claim; the statute was not identified.
succession.foreign_law_note: Movables follow the law of the deceased's domicile, immovables follow Gibraltar law. There is no choice of nationality law.
succession.trust_note: Hague Convention extended to Gibraltar (1 January 1992 per a Dutch treaty record). Foundations are governed by the Gibraltar private foundations law of 2017; its exact title was not verified.

assumptions: The family is ordinarily resident (183 days in the year or 300 days over three years) and, for Category 2, was not present over 183 days in any of the previous five years and has no Gibraltar business or employment.

The portfolio is of shares listed on exchanges the Commissioner has designated as Recognised Stock Exchanges, or of companies whose profits Gibraltar did not tax; the designating Gazette notice was not found.

No structure is modelled: a resident individual already pays no tax on foreign listed dividends, interest or gains, so a Gibraltar company, trust or foundation could not lower the tax; Gibraltar companies are taxed on Gibraltar-source income only and would add running costs.

Ordinary residence also needs a right to reside (a Gibraltar residence permit or a Category 2 certificate); post-Brexit rules for EU nationals were not researched, so the standard path is shown as if open.
Category 2: one certificate and one minimum for the family by the Rule 11 election; the GBP 5 million net-assets requirement (announced 18 June 2026) is met by a GBP 30 million portfolio.
Stamp duty on buying the EUR 5 million home (up to 4.5% on the part above GBP 800,000, PwC) is a one-off cost and is not modelled.
open_questions: The Gazette notice designating Recognised Stock Exchanges was not found; para (iv) of Table C Class 1(a) would exempt foreign dividends out of untaxed profits in any case.
The Estate Duties (Repeal and Consequential Provisions) Act 1997 could not be opened (404); the no-estate-duty statement rests on PwC.
The Category 2 net-assets figure (GBP 5 million) is announced policy; the Rules contain no figure (press release 469/2026).

Rule 11 lets the holder elect that the spouse's and children's income be deemed his; whether a separate certificate (Rule 11(5)) would cost a second GBP 37,000 minimum is not stated in the Rules and was not verified.

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary residence)
paths.note: An ordinarily resident individual is taxed on foreign 'other income' (Income Tax Act 2010 s. 11(2)), but dividends from listed companies or out of profits Gibraltar did not tax are excluded (Sch. 1 Table C Class 1(a)(iii)-(iv)); no tax on interest or capital gains, no wealth or inheritance tax. A foreign portfolio therefore bears no Gibraltar tax.

paths.name: Category 2 high-net-worth individual
paths.note: Certificate under the Qualifying (Category 2) Individuals Rules 2004: foreign dividends are outside assessable income (Rule 10(1)), assessable income is capped at GBP 118,000, and the minimum tax is GBP 37,000 a year (Rule 9(4)(b)), which is the whole tax for a passive foreign portfolio. A spouse and children can be covered by election (Rule 11). It costs GBP 37,000 more than ordinary residence; it is relevant as a residence route and for certainty. Net assets GBP 5 million for new applicants from June 2026.

immigration.name: Gibraltar
immigration.summary: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory outside the EU and EEA and controls its own immigration. EU and British citizens have no free movement there, and since 6 October 2025 new residence applications from EEA and British citizens are suspended unless an exception applies. For everyone the practical routes are a job-based residence permit (average-salary contract of about GBP 37,500, a Gibraltar employer and housing), HEPSS for executives paid over GBP 160,000, or Category 2 for people with net wealth of GBP 5 million and approved housing. The EU-UK Gibraltar Agreement applies provisionally from 15 July 2026 but creates no residence right.
immigration.naturalisation: Permanent residency after 10 years (raised from 5 by the Gibraltarian Status and Immigration (Amendment) Bill 2025) and Gibraltarian status by long residence after 20 years (was 10), at ministerial discretion. Whether the Bill is enacted was not confirmed from legislation.

routes.name: Category 2 individual (high net worth)
routes.limited_places: discretionary: status is awarded on the decision of the Finance Centre Director
routes.summary: Wealthy individuals with exclusive use of approved Gibraltar housing can be certified as Category 2, which caps their Gibraltar income tax and gives the right to live in Gibraltar. No right to the status: it is awarded at the Director's discretion.
routes.requirements: Qualifying (Category 2) Individuals Rules 2004. For new applicants after the June 2026 change: minimum net wealth GBP 5 million (was GBP 2 million); exclusive use of approved Category 2 property (bought or rented; guideline from GBP 550,000 to buy or GBP 2,500 a month to rent); no competing local business activity unless approved; restrictions if the applicant lived or worked in Gibraltar in the previous five years. Existing holders keep the old thresholds. A tax deposit equal to the maximum annual Category 2 tax (GBP 42,380) is paid on application. Category 2 gives no entitlement to publicly funded schooling or healthcare, and losing the status ends the right to remain. Effective date of the GBP 5 million threshold is not stated in the press release.
routes.fees_note: Application fee GBP 5,000 (was GBP 1,233) per the government; plus a refundable tax deposit of GBP 42,380 (adviser guide, 2026-27).
routes.physical_presence: None required for Category 2 status (adviser guide); being a Category 2 does not prevent tax residence elsewhere
routes.family: Spouse and family income may be included in the assessment; adviser guide.
routes.tax_note: Income tax only on the first GBP 118,000 of assessable income: maximum GBP 42,380, minimum GBP 37,000 a year (2026-27, adviser guide). No capital gains, wealth, gift or inheritance tax. The tax year runs 1 July to 30 June. A residence permit does not stop you being tax resident elsewhere.

routes.name: High Executive Possessing Specialist Skills (HEPSS)
routes.limited_places: discretionary: the Finance Centre certifies only skills Gibraltar does not have
routes.summary: A Gibraltar employer applies for a certificate for a senior executive with scarce skills paid over GBP 160,000 a year. The holder gets a capped tax rate.
routes.requirements: High Executive Possessing Specialist Skills Rules 2008, application form effective August 2026: skills necessary for economic activity of particular value to Gibraltar and not available there; a high executive or senior management post earning more than GBP 160,000 a year in Gibraltar; exclusive use of approved residential accommodation; not gainfully occupied or resident in Gibraltar in the 36 months before the application year (the Minister for Finance may waive this). Two references (one from a bank), proof of earnings, passport copy and CV. Employer applies for the certificate. Advisers report the 2026 residence criteria do not apply to HEPSS holders; not confirmed in an official text.
routes.fees_note: Application fee GBP 1,264, non-refundable, per the 2026 form.
routes.physical_presence: Not published on the form; accommodation in Gibraltar must be available for the certificate period
routes.tax_note: Tax is capped on the first GBP 160,000 of income; the exact capped amount was not sourced from an official page (advisers conflict).

routes.name: Residence permit for employees (new criteria, June 2026)
routes.summary: Anyone who has a job with an established Gibraltar employer and housing in Gibraltar can apply for an annual residence permit. The Treaty gives no automatic right to live or work in Gibraltar.
routes.requirements: Government residence criteria framework announced 17 June 2026; regulations were still being drafted then. As summarised by advisers: contract at or above average gross annual earnings (about GBP 37,500, updated yearly; waivable under 30 if the employer pays equivalent tax and social insurance); employer trading in or from Gibraltar for at least a year and fully compliant; purchased home for exclusive use or a rental of at least 12 months as primary residence; applicant generally 55 or under; home-country vetting certificate; only spouse and children may accompany. New businesses and first-time self-employed pay a refundable deposit. Permits renew annually and lapse 8 weeks after notice of termination or if tax or social insurance stops. Rules apply to people seeking residence after 6 October 2025. For EEA and British citizens see the suspension route.
routes.fees_note: Application GBP 250, renewal GBP 100 (adviser summary of the policy, not an official text); fine up to GBP 2,500 for residing without a permit.
routes.physical_presence: Genuine residence tied to the job and Gibraltar accommodation; no day count found
routes.family: Spouse (needs a payment equal to the maximum employee social insurance contribution) and children; covered by the Group Practice Medical Scheme; children can attend Gibraltar schools.
routes.tax_note: Taxed in Gibraltar on employment income under normal rules; a permit does not decide tax residence elsewhere.

routes.name: EEA and British citizens' residence rights (registration certificate, suspended for new applicants)
routes.status_note: Immigration (EU Exit) Regulations 2025 of 6 October 2025 suspended new residence rights for EEA nationals, including British citizens, until lifted by Order of the Chief Minister; no lifting found by 17 October 2026.
routes.summary: Gibraltar is outside the EU, and since 6 October 2025 it grants no new residence documents to EEA or British citizens except in listed cases. People who held a registration certificate or residence card before that date keep their rights.
routes.requirements: Section 55NA of the Immigration, Asylum and Refugee Act (added October 2025): the right to reside for more than three months is suspended unless the person held a registration certificate, residence card or permanent residence document by 6 October 2025; applications filed before that date are still processed; the Chief Minister can approve exceptions (international obligations, hardship, economic reasons). The EU-UK Gibraltar Agreement, provisionally applied from 15 July 2026, gives no automatic right to reside or work in Gibraltar. EU citizens elsewhere in the EU have no free movement into Gibraltar. British citizens: no Common Travel Area style right to settle was found; they appear within the suspension.
